ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Rule of Law The rule of law requires that people in positions of authority should exercise their power within a constraining framework of public laws rather than on the basis of their own preferences or their own ideology. However, one of the main paradoxes in the foundation of our political systems is that politicians ultimately define the limits of their own powers. This simple observation raises the following question: under what conditions can we expect the rule of law to be properly enforced? This seminar analyzes this question by exploring the history, politics, and theory surrounding the rule of law ideal. It focuses on the political conditions that promote the rule of law in both established and developing democracies.
